You write the final report of a trial-autopsy system for an analyst. Plain language, precise,
no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,
use the source title given for that fact_id in the Facts list. State uncertainty honestly.

Return JSON only:
{"headline": "<one sentence verdict>",

 "key_evidence": ["<short bullet with the number and its source title>", "..."],
 "what_would_change_this": "<one or two sentences>",
 "readthrough_note": "<one or two sentences on other programmes, or empty>"}

response: {"headline": "GISSI-HF found rosuvastatin 10 mg daily had no effect on all-cause mortality (HR 1.00, 95% CI 0.898–1.122, p=0.943) or the composite of death/CV hospitalization (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.908–1.112, p=0.903) in 4,574 patients with symptomatic chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV) over 3.9 years, confirming that LDL-C lowering does not translate into benefit in advanced HF where pump failure and arrhythmia dominate mortality.", "summary": "The trial randomized 4,574 patients with chronic heart failure of any cause to rosuvastatin 10 mg or placebo in a factorial design with n-3 PUFA. The primary endpoints — all-cause mortality and death or CV hospitalization — showed hazard ratios of 1.00 and 1.01 with tight confidence intervals excluding the prespecified 15% and 20% relative risk reductions. The calculator cannot compute an expected effect because on-treatment LDL-C change was not measured in the trial. However, the neutral result aligns with the contemporaneous CORONA trial (rosuvastatin in ischemic systolic HF, HR 0.92, p=0.12) and reflects a population mismatch: in advanced HF, most deaths are from pump failure and sudden arrhythmia, not atherosclerotic events that LDL-C lowering prevents. The drug appeared safe. Confidence in this qualitative diagnosis is high despite the calculator's 'insufficient_data' output.", "key_evidence": ["HR 1.00 for all-cause mortality (95% CI 0.898–1.122, p=0.943) — The GISSI-HF Trial: Effects of Rosuvastatin in 4,574 Patients with Chronic Heart Failure", "HR 1.01 for death/CV hospitalization (95% CI 0.908–1.112, p=0.903) — The GISSI-HF Trial: Effects of Rosuvastatin in 4,574 Patients with Chronic Heart Failure", "4,574 patients randomized, median follow-up 3.9 years, 1,301 deaths observed vs 1,252 planned — The GISSI-HF Trial: Effects of Rosuvastatin in 4,574 Patients with Chronic Heart Failure; Rationale and design of the GISSI heart failure trial...", "Prespecified target: 15% RRR in mortality, 20% RRR in composite; MDE HR at 80% power = 0.856 — Rationale and design of the GISSI heart failure trial...; Calculator", "Population: symptomatic CHF NYHA class II–IV (advanced HF) — ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00336336", "CORONA trial (rosuvastatin 10 mg in ischemic systolic HF, 33-month follow-up) also neutral on primary endpoint — Randomized clinical outcome trials of statins in heart failure", "LDL-C change not measured in GISSI-HF (calculator weakest_link) — Calculator", "Readout: 'rosuvastatin... did not affect clinical outcomes... the drug seemed to be safe' — The GISSI-HF Trial: Effects of Rosuvastatin in 4,574 Patients with Chronic Heart Failure"], "what_would_change_this": "Measured on-treatment LDL-C change in GISSI-HF participants would allow the calculator to quantify the expected effect; a subgroup analysis showing benefit in ischemic-etiology patients or those with higher baseline LDL-C would challenge the population-mismatch explanation.", "readthrough_note": ""}
